title: Studying the microglia response to oxidized phosphatidylcholine in primary mouse neuron culture and mouse spinal cord
protocol: Coat T25 tissue culture flasks with 5 mL of 10 μg/mL poly-L-ornithine dissolved in sterile distilled water for at least 30 min at 22°C–24°C.
Remove the poly-L-ornithine solution and wash the flasks with sterile distilled water.
Coat 96-well flat bottom black/clear plates with poly-L-ornithine solution.
Prepare growth medium containing Neurobasal Plus medium and 1X B27 Plus Supplement at 37°C.
Prewarm approximately 300 mL of water in a 1 L beaker to 35°C–38°C on a hot plate.
Disinfect instruments with 70% ethanol: dissection scissors, forceps, iridectomy scissors, ultra-fine point forceps, and scalpel.
Autoclave 100 mL bottles and Buchner funnel with nylon mesh at 130 μm pore size.
Acquire cortical neurons from mouse embryos at gestation days 14–16.
Euthanize pregnant mouse with ketamine (100 mg/mg)/xylazine (10 mg/kg) overdose via intraperitoneal injection.
Disinfect the abdominal area with 70% ethanol.
Make a V-shaped incision in the skin of the lower abdomen with scissors.
Disinfect the instruments with 70% ethanol.
Lift the uterine horns containing the embryos and dissect them out of the abdominal cavity.
Place the uterine horns in a sterile 10-cm petri dish containing calcium and magnesium-free Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (CMF-HBSS).
Dissect the uterine horns to release the embryos from their individual sacs.
Cut around the base of the head of each embryo with iridectomy scissors.
Scoop out the brain into a new sterile 10-cm petri dish containing 20 mL CMF-HBSS.
Remove the meninges from the brains using a dissection microscope.
Separate the cerebral hemispheres and place them in a new sterile 10-cm petri dish containing 3–5 mL of CMF-HBSS.
Dice the cerebral hemispheres with a sterile scalpel into fragments of <1 mm.
Form a tissue suspension by adding 10–15 mL of CMF-HBSS to the diced cerebral hemispheres.
Transfer the tissue suspension into an autoclaved 100-mL bottle using a sterile pipette.
Note the volume transferred.
Add sterile trypsin to the tissue suspension to a final concentration of 0.025%.
Immerse the 100 mL bottle containing the tissue suspension in the prewarmed water bath at 35°C–38°C.
Set the stirring speed to low medium and homogenize the tissue for 15 min at 35°C–38°C.
Add 1 mL of sterile heat-inactivated FBS to the homogenized suspension to inactivate the trypsin.
Pour the suspension through a Buchner filter funnel with nylon mesh into a new autoclaved 100 mL bottle.
Using the plunger of a 3 mL syringe, gently grind the tissue on the nylon mesh and wash it through the filter with CMF-HBSS.
Transfer the filtered tissue suspension to 50 mL tubes and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 22°C–24°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellets in CMF-HBSS, pooling all the cell suspensions in one 50 mL tube.
Top up with CMF-HBSS to 50 mL and centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 22°C–24°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 5–10 mL of prewarmed growth medium.
Count cells with trypan blue for culturing.
Culture neurons in preparation for microglia co-culture.
Seed 20 × 10^6 cells isolated from step 3 per PO-coated T25 flask from step 1 in 5 mL of growth medium.
Incubate cells at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 95% air and 5% CO2.
After 2–3 days, healthy neurons have grown processes and can be harvested for experimental use.
Add trypsin to the neuron culture to a final concentration of 0.25%.
Incubate at 37°C for ∼ 5 min to dislodge the neurons.
Then add 0.5 mL of sterile heat inactivated FBS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 22°C–24°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend in 5 mL of prewarmed growth medium.
Count cells with trypan blue.
Seed the neurons into PO coated 96-well flat bottom black/clear plates from step 1 at 0.75–1 × 10^5 cells per well in 100 μL of growth medium.
After 24–48 h, neurons with healthy process formation in 96-well plates can be co-cultured with microglia.
Disinfect dissection tools with 70% ethanol: dissection scissors, forceps, iridectomy scissors, small dissecting spatula, scalpel.
Harvest brains from mice.
Prepare sample preparation medium of CMF-HBSS containing 2% FBS and 1 mM EDTA.
Prewarm brain digestion medium containing CMF-HBSS with 20 units/mL of Papain (Worthington) and 100 μg/mL DNase I to 22°C–24°C.
Combine 9 parts of Percoll (Sigma) with 1 part of 10X D-PBS to make a 100% isotonic Percoll solution.
Combine 3 parts of 100% isotonic Percoll with 7 parts of sample preparation medium to create 6 mL of 30% Percoll solution per brain.
Euthanize mice with ketamine (100 mg/kg) / xylazine (10 mg/kg) overdose via intraperitoneal injection.
Disinfect mouse with 70% ethanol.
Decapitate the mouse using dissection scissors.
Cut along the top of the skull and parallel on both sides using iridectomy scissors.
Peel away the skin and top of the skull using forceps.
Scoop out the brain using a dissecting spatula.
Place the brain in a sterile petri dish containing 1 mL of brain digestion medium.
Mince the brains with a scalpel into small pieces < 1 mm.
Transfer the minced brain tissue into a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the petri dish with the remaining brain digestion medium and add to the cell suspension in the 50 mL tube.
Incubate the cell suspension at 37°C for 30 min while continuously shaking or rotating at medium low speed.
Filter the digested brain tissue through a 70 μm nylon mesh strainer using the rubber end of a syringe plunger.
Rinse the strainer with sample preparation medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 10 min with low brakes.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant with a serological pipette.
Add 30% Percoll prepared in step 5d to the cell pellet.
Centrifuge at 700 × g for 10 minutes with no brakes.
Use a 2 mL serological pipette to carefully remove the upper myelin layer.
Carefully discard the remaining supernatant.
Transfer cells to a new tube and top up with sample preparation medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 minutes with low brakes.
Discard the supernatants.
Count cells with trypan blue.
Resuspend cells at 2.5 × 10^7 cells/mL in PBS containing 2% FBS and 1 mM EDTA.
Enrich CD11b+ microglia from cells isolated from brains using the EasySep™ Mouse CD11b Positive Selection Kit II.
Perform steps according to the manufacturer’s protocol, using the EasySepTM magnet.
Resuspend enriched cells in neuron growth medium.
Count resuspended cells with trypan blue.
Add 2.5 × 10^4 microglia resuspended in 100 μL of neuron growth medium to each well containing 0.75–1 × 10^5 neurons.
Coculture microglia and neurons in a total volume of 200 μL of neuron growth medium.
Incubate cocultured microglia and neurons for 24 or 48 hours as required.
Prepare 3–4 technical replicate wells per experimental condition.
Ensure microglia and neurons have been in coculture for at least 24 hours.
Include neurons alone as a control condition.
Include untreated microglia and neurons as another control condition.
Add purified OxPCs to the cells at desired concentrations.
Carefully remove 100 μL of media from each well.
Add 100 μL of neural basal plus medium containing twice the concentration of OxPCs for a final 1:2 dilution.
Include equivalent volume of ethanol used to dissolve the OxPCs as a control in neurons alone and neurons cocultured with microglia.
Include equivalent concentrations of DPPC as OxPCs as a control in neurons alone and neuron cocultured with microglia.
Incubate cells at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 95% air and 5% CO2.
Optional: Add cell viability dyes such as Calcein AM or propidium iodide at manufacturer’s recommended concentrations to OxPC treated neurons for live tracking and imaging of neurotoxicity over time.
Optional: Treat cells with modulators of interest, such as cytochalasin D or latrunculin A, according to the experiment requirements.
Remove 100 μL of neuron growth medium from cells if testing microglia phagocytosis is needed for neuronal protection against OxPCs.
Add 50 μL of neural basal medium containing 20 μM cytochalasin D or 800 nM latrunculin A to the cells and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Add 50 μL of neural basal plus medium alone, with 4X the concentration of OxPCs for a final 1:4 dilution, after removing cytochalasin D or latrunculin A.
Incubate cells for 24 h after adding OxPC treatments.
Remove tissue culture supernatant and fix cells for immunochemistry and quantitative fluorescence microscopy.
Store tissue culture supernatant at -80°C for additional secretome analysis if necessary.
Add 100 μL of 4% PFA to the cells and incubate for 10 min at 22-24°C after removing the supernatant.
Carefully pipette to remove the PFA, then wash twice with 100 μL of PBS.
Permeabilize cells with 100 μL PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 10 minutes at 22°C–24°C.
Carefully pipette to remove the supernatant.
Block cells by adding 100 μL of Odyssey Blocking Buffer and incubate for 1 hour at 22°C–24°C.
Remove the blocking buffer.
Incubate with 70 μL of primary antibodies diluted in the blocking buffer for 8–12 hours at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Use mouse anti-tubulin β3 IgG (clone TUJ1) at 2 μg/mL to label neurons.
Use rabbit anti-IBA1 IgG (polyclonal) at 0.5–0.7 μg/mL to label microglia.
Remove the supernatant and wash twice with 100 μL of PBS.
Incubate with 70 μL of secondary antibodies and DAPI diluted in blocking buffer for 0.5–1 hour at 22°C–24°C with gentle shaking.
Use Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-rabbit IgG at 1:400 from manufacturer’s recommended stock concentration.
Use DAPI at 1 μg/mL.
Remove the supernatant, wash twice with 100 μL of PBS.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of PBS.
Image cells using a 10×/0.5 NA air or a 20× 0.45 NA air objective on the ImageXpress Micro XLS High-Content Analysis System.
Capture 9 to 12 imaging fields evenly distributed across each well per experimental condition.
Use detection filters: DAPI excitation 387/11 – emission 447/60; Alexa Fluor 488 excitation 482/35 – emission 536/40; and Alexa Fluor 647 excitation 628/40 – emission 692/40.
Save all raw data files for analysis and record keeping.
Induce OxPC-mediated neurodegeneration in the spinal cord white matter of microglia-sufficient mice.
Induce OxPC-mediated neurodegeneration in the spinal cord white matter of microglia-deficient mice.
Purify OxPCs for injection.
Stereotaxically inject purified OxPCs into the ventral spinal cord white matter of mice.
Inject 100 μL of PBS intraperitoneally in tamoxifen pre-treated CX3CR1CreER:Rosa26iDTR mice as controls.
Prepare a solution containing 1 μg of diphtheria toxin (DT) in 100 μL of PBS.
Intraperitoneally inject the DT-containing solution into tamoxifen pre-treated CX3CR1CreER:Rosa26iDTR mice for microglia depletion.
Prepare the surgery.
Prepare the needle and the syringe.
Place a 32-gauge Hamilton needle on a 10 μL Hamilton syringe.
Clean syringe in the following order with autoclaved 20 μL ddH2O, PBS, and acetate.
Draw desired volume of PBS (sham controls) or OxPC (POVPC or PAzePC dissolved in PBS at 10 mg/mL) into syringe, be careful to avoid bubbles.
Place syringe onto the stereotaxic instrument.
Sterilize the following tools using microbead sterilizer at 120°C–130°C: #15 scalpel blade and scalpel Micro dissecting spring scissors Tissue spreader
Anesthetize a mouse with 100 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg xylazine.
Clean and prepare the surgical site.
Use a shaver to remove hair from the ears to midback, revealing the surgical site.
Clean the surgical site with 70% ethanol using a gauze pad.
Apply iodine to disinfect the surgical site.
Apply ophthalmic gel to prevent eyes from drying out.
Place the mouse onto the stereotaxic instrument dorsal side up once it reaches a surgical plane of anesthesia.
Use a heating pad underneath or heating lamp overhead to maintain the mouse’s body temperature.
Elevate the midsection for easier access to the thoracic spinal region.
Make a 2 cm incision between the shoulder blades using a #15 scalpel.
Pull apart the skin and fat pads underneath using two forceps.
Use a spreader to firmly keep the skin and fat pads apart to expose the underlying musculature.
Find the T2 vertebrae using forceps.
Count down caudally to find the T3-T4 gap.
Use micro dissecting spring scissors and forceps to blunt dissect apart the musculature to expose the spinal cord at the T3-T4 gap.
Use a 30-gauge needle to carefully prick and remove the meningeal layer.
Absorb potential blood or cerebral spinal fluid with eye spears to keep the operating area clear.
Inject OxPCs into the T3-T4 gap.
Stereotactically angle the Hamilton syringe and needle to 0.5 degrees.
Align the syringe over the T3-T4 gap with removed meninges.
Lower the needle tip until it is contacting the spinal cord dorsal surface slightly to the right side of the midline.
Note the position of the needle using the graded measurements on the Z-direction stereotaxic arm as the baseline.
From the baseline subtract 1.3 mm to reach the ventral white matter.
Using the Z-direction arm control, make a quick downward motion to insert the needle into the spinal cord.
Slowly lower the needle until the baseline minus 1.3 mm position.
Use the micromanipulator to inject 0.5 μL of PBS (sham control) or OxPC at a rate of 0.25 μL/min.
Leave the needle in place for 2 min to avoid backflow.
Carefully retract the needle from the spinal cord.
Make a single interrupted suture in the muscle/adipose tissue over the spinal column using vicryl suture.
Suture the skin using uninterrupted vicryl sutures or staples.
Provide any post-operative analgesic required by institutional animal care regulations.
Place animals in heated recovery chamber until they regain conscious movement.
Monitor animals for open sutures and as required by institutional animal care regulations.
Inject DT or PBS intraperitoneally following spinal cord surgery to compare neurodegeneration with or without microglia deficiency as needed.
Euthanize mouse with ketamine/xylazine overdose via intraperitoneal injection.
Perfuse the mouse via cardiac puncture.
Disinfect the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Lay the mouse on its back and make an incision around the middle abdomen to expose the diaphragm.
Remove the right kidney of the mouse.
Cut open the diaphragm to access the heart.
Insert a 15 mL syringe with 26½ gauge needle containing 15 mL of PBS into the right ventricle of the heart.
Push the syringe slowly and perfuse the mouse with ∼15 mL of PBS.
Dissect and remove the spinal cord.
Turn the mouse to lay on its front, pin its nose, arms, and legs to a dissecting board so the mouse’s head and spinal cord are lying flat.
Remove the skin from the upper lumber area to the head.
Cut to remove excess muscles and fat along the back and arms.
Cut through the skull from the front end, then on both sides through the top of the skull using dissecting scissors.
Carefully cut and remove the dorsal skull and vertebrae with iridectomy scissors to expose the brain and spinal cord.
Gently lift the brain up with thick forceps and cut along both sides of the spinal cords to free it from the vertebra column.
Trim the spinal cord to collect the lower cervical and thoracic regions containing the lesion site.
Place the spinal cord piece on a segment of thick filter paper and submerge into 4% PFA in 1.6 mL microfuge tubes for 8–12 h fixation at 4°C.
Transfer spinal cord tissue from PFA to 30% sucrose solution for incubation for at least 48 hours.
Freeze spinal cords in cryo embedding molds along with control tissues for better consistency.
Submerge spinal cord segments in molds containing FSC 22 Frozen Section Media (Leica).
Align spinal cords evenly in parallel.
Transfer the mold with tissues onto a dewar containing dry ice and isopentane.
Cover until it forms a completely frozen tissue block.
Store frozen tissue blocks at −20°C for up to a week before cryosectioning.
For long-term storage, store at −80°C.
Warm spinal cords from −80°C storage to −20°C in the cryostat before cutting.
Label 20 microscope slides appropriately with experimental parameters.
Cut the tissue block coronally into 20 μm sections sequentially onto slides starting at slide #1.
Separate coronal sections (in columns going down) on each slide by 400 μm for each spinal cord lesion.
Store cut tissue sections on microscope slides at −20°C for up to 6 months, or at −80°C for longer prior to analysis.
Stain spinal cord lesion with E06 antibody to detect OxPC deposition.
Stain spinal cord lesion with CD68 antibody to detect microglia/macrophages.
Stain spinal cord lesion with IBA1 antibody to detect microglia/macrophages.
Stain spinal cord lesion with neurofilament heavy chain antibody to detect axons and neurodegeneration.
Stain spinal cord lesion with myelin basic protein antibody to detect myelin and its disruption.
Treat spinal cord tissues successively with citrisolv, isopropanol, and various concentrations of ethanol.
Wash spinal cord tissues with distilled water for 1 minute.
Incubate spinal cord tissues in eriochrome cyanine staining solution for 15 minutes.
Wash spinal cord tissues with ddH2O for 1 minute followed by 0.5% NH4OH for 5–10 seconds, then again with ddH2O for 1 minute.
Incubate spinal cord tissues with 1% neutral red solution for 2 minutes.
Dehydrate spinal cord tissues through successive washes of various concentrations of ethanol and isopropanol.
Mount the slide with coverslips using Acrytol mounting medium.
Acquire images of serial spinal cord lesions using the Olympus VS110 Slidescanner.
Analyze demyelinated areas in the ventral spinal cord white matter for lesion size and volume using appropriate software such as ImageJ or cellSens.
Thaw spinal cord tissue slides to 22°C–24°C and air dry.
Submerge tissues in PBS for 10 minutes at 22°C–24°C.
Gently tap the slides to dry them.
Permeabilize the spinal cord sections by covering with 800 μL of PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 10 minutes at 22°C–24°C.
Gently tap the slides to dry them.
Cover the tissue sections with 800 μL of horse blocking solution (PBS, 10% horse serum, 1% BSA, 0.1% cold fish stain gelation, 0.1% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20) for 1 hour at 22°C–24°C.
Wash the slides once by briefly submerging in PBS and gently tap dry.
Cover the tissue sections with 600 μL of primary antibodies resuspended in antibody dilution buffer (PBS, 1% BSA, 0.1% cold fish stain gelation, 0.1% Triton X-100) for 8–12 hours at 4°C.
If using mouse-derived antibodies, add rat anti-CD16/32 Fc blocking antibody (BD Biosciences) at 5 μg/mL to the blocking solution.
Ensure there is no overlap in the hosts of the primary antibodies.
Block tissues with rat anti-CD16/32 Fc blocking antibody if necessary.
Wash tissue sections three times with PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 for 5 min each at 22°C–24°C.
Cover tissue sections with 600 μL of secondary antibodies and DAPI (1 μg/mL) resuspended in antibody dilution buffer for 1 h at 22°C–24°C.
Include a slide stained only with secondary antibodies and DAPI to assess non-specific binding.
Wash tissue sections three times with PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 for 5 min each at 22°C–24°C.
Mount slides with coverslips using Fluoromount-G solution (SouthernBiotech).
Air dry slides at 22°C–24°C for approximately 1 hour.
Store stained slides in the dark at 4°C for at least 2 weeks prior to microscopy analysis.
Acquire z-stacks of the lesion epicenters using a Leica TCS Sp8 laser confocal microscope.
Use a 25X 0.5 NA water objective for imaging.
Employ 405 nm, 71 nm, 552 nm, and 640 nm excitation lasers for labeled secondary antibodies and DAPI.
Utilize two low dark current Hamamatsu PMT detectors and two high sensitivity hybrid detectors.
Acquire images in 8-bits format in a z-stack using uni-directional scanning.
Apply 1 times frame averaging during image acquisition.
Set the pinhole to 1 airy unit.
Use 0.75× zoom for imaging.
Capture each optical section at 0.57 μm intervals.
Maintain an xy resolution of 2048 × 2048 pixels.
Save all raw data in Tiff and project files for analysis and record keeping.
Ensure equal acquisition settings are applied to all samples within each set of experiments.
Apply consistent laser, gain, and offset settings across all samples.
